title: How do we fill blanks by how terms change?
description: Two equations with blanks are completed by reasoning about how each term changes, without working out the sums. The second answer is checked by working out both sides.
teaching_notes: Let the child try first, then compare. One idea: when one term goes up by some amount, the other part must change to keep both sides equal. Ask the child to say how much each number went up or down.

video_script.why: The child fills the blanks by asking how much each number has changed, as in the known sum with two changing terms.
video_script.substitution: The same reasoning works with other numbers: find how much a term went up or down, then balance it.
video_script.anchor: two equations with blanks, with a number line below
video_script.payoff_line: Find how much each number changed, then balance it.

final_answer.spoken: four hundred and nineteen in the left blank and four hundred and twenty three in the right blank, and seventy one

maths_rules: 423 + 419 = 419 + 423: the same two terms in a different order, so both sides are equal
423 is 4 more than 419, so the blank beside 419 must be 4 more than the blank beside 423; any such pair works
210 is 3 more than 207, so the number taken away must be 3 more than 68, which is 71
video_script.design: One idea: find how much each number changed, then balance it. The two equations stay in the anchor band; the working band shows each change. No hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check the second equation.
Two hundred and seven minus sixty eight is one hundred and thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two hundred and ten minus seventy one is also one hundred and thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Both sides match.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Find how much each number changed, then balance it.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first blanks are four hundred and nineteen and four hundred and twenty three.
